capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction.

- The first claim is the standard extensionality principle for bundled affine subspaces: an `AffineSubspace` is determined by its underlying set, so the `SetLike.coe` map is injective.

- For the second, use the affine-span representation
  \[
  \operatorname{vectorSpan}_k(s)=(\operatorname{affineSpan}_k(s)).\operatorname{direction}.
  \]
  Given \(v\in s-ᵥs\), write \(v=p-ᵥq\) with \(p,q\in s\). Both points lie in `affineSpan k s`; the difference of two points of an affine subspace belongs to its direction. Hence \(v\in\operatorname{vectorSpan}_k(s)\).

Thus the only intermediate facts needed are `s ⊆ affineSpan k s` and closure of an affine subspace’s direction under differences of its points. No stronger field assumption is required; the ring/module/torsor structure suffices.
